findings.title: Light-theme value for embedded-post username changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The conversion wrote `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, i.e. the light-theme branch was changed from 30% to 70%. On a normal light scheme the bolded username in expanded/in-reply-to posts goes from a dark gray to a very light gray on a white background, badly reducing contrast/readability. The light branch should stay at 30% (with 70% for the dark branch) to keep the previous appearance.

findings.title: Topic-map heading light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value jumps from 20% to 50%, so on mobile the topic-map heading becomes noticeably lighter than before and no longer matches the desktop rule (which keeps 20%/80%). The light branch should remain 20% with 80% for dark to preserve existing appearance and desktop/mobile parity.

findings.title: custom-message-length light-theme lightness inverted (70% -> 30%)
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The two arguments look swapped: the light-theme value went from 70% to 30%, making the hint text much darker on mobile, and it no longer matches `desktop/modal.scss` which uses 70%/30%. Use 70% for light and 30% for dark.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light value changed 30% -> 50%, now identical to .title
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`. Besides lightening the name in light themes, it makes `.name` and `.title` exactly the same color, removing the intended visual distinction between the member name and their title. The light branch should remain 30% (with 70% for dark).

findings.title: group-member-info .name light value changed 30% -> 50% (mobile)
findings.body: Same regression as in `desktop/user.scss`: `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and now resolves to 50% in light themes, identical to the adjacent `.title` rule, so member name and title are no longer visually distinguishable and the name is lighter than before. Light branch should stay at 30%, dark branch 70%.

findings.title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification still uses scale-color($primary)
findings.body: Every other dim-text rule in this file was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, ...), scale-color($secondary, ...))`, but `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. On dark schemes `$primary` is light, so lightening it by 50% produces near-white text instead of the intended dimmed color, leaving this element inconsistent with the rest of the list after this PR.

findings.title: #file-uploading uses lightened $secondary unconditionally
findings.body: `#reply-control #file-uploading { color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%); }` lightens the background color for all schemes. In a light scheme `$secondary` is near-white, so the uploading text is nearly invisible against the composer background. Given the adjacent rules in this hunk were converted to `dark-light-choose(...)`, this one should be converted too (primary-based value for light, secondary-based for dark).

findings.title: Stale comment referencing the old topic-list default color
findings.body: The comment above the coldmap rules still says "the default for table cells in topic list is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)", but after this PR the topic-list cell color is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The comment now documents a value that no longer exists and will mislead anyone tuning these colors.
